title: Remember the 2009 Flight Control game? I built a parking lot version in Godot 4 using antigravity
author: Maximum-Policy-8340
selftext:
Hey everyone! 👋

I was feeling really nostalgic recently for the classic line-drawing game Flight Control from the early mobile days. As someone looking to try Godot 4, I challenged myself to build a small, fun project around that exact same rush: Park Control 2D.

Instead of landing planes on runways, you are running a chaotic parking lot where you drag paths for incoming cars into bays, route departing vehicles to the exit gate, and reroute cars mid-flight to prevent disastrous pile-ups!

What I learned building this in Godot:

* Dynamic Path Drawing: Drawing real-time routes with Line2D and letting players click moving vehicles to steer them out of harm's way.
* Special Vehicles and Rules: Added priority Ambulances (sirens and strobes), VIP Limos, and dedicated EV Charging Stalls (standard cars can park there, but EVs get hit with an immediate fine if they are parked outside of an EV spot!).
* Atmosphere: Dynamic Day to Dusk to Night lighting with CanvasModulate and active headlights and taillights.
* Audio: 100% procedurally synthesized audio so the web export loads instantly with zero external audio assets.

Free to Play (No Download Needed): The game is completely free:

* Play in Browser: [https://parkcontrol.inventkid.com](https://parkcontrol.inventkid.com/)

This was purely a fun learning project for me, but if you take it for a spin on your coffee break and have a good time, you can always support me on buy me a coffee (link on website)

I would love to hear your thoughts or feedback on the mechanics and game feel. Thank you
